items.t: Hope is a district municipality in the Fraser Valley Regional District at the confluence of the Fraser and Coquihalla rivers, at the eastern end of the Fraser Valley where the Fraser Canyon begins. Its named areas are the townsite grid (Wallace Street downtown spine, Park Street, 7th Avenue), Silver Creek (west), Kawkawa Lake (east), and Flood/Laidlaw (west fringe, where most manufactured-home parks line Flood-Hope Road).

Where condo stock concentrates: it barely exists to concentrate. Hope's strata stock is three named complexes — one form-conflicted low-rise on Scott Drive and two townhouse complexes on Douglas Street and 7th Avenue — inside a housing market the District's own numbers describe as mostly single-family: permits from 2021 to October 2024 were mostly single-family dwellings (70 units) plus suites (22). The townsite core around Wallace Street holds what apartment and townhouse product exists; Silver Creek is rancher-style family homes and Kawkawa Lake is recreational properties.

Population context (2021 Census): 6,686 people (+8.2% from 6,181 in 2016), 3,243 total private dwellings, 2,939 occupied by usual residents, median age 54.8 — an older-than-average town, which is why its rental and care ladder is as large as it is relative to its size.

Schools (SD78 Fraser-Cascade): Coquihalla Elementary (K–6, 455 6th Ave, ~350 students) takes the old Town of Hope, east to Sumallo Lodge including Kawkawa Lake/Othello, west to Ruby Creek, plus Spuzzum and Yale; Silver Creek Elementary (K–7) takes Silver Creek and west of it; Hope Secondary School (Gr. 7–12, 444 Stuart St) takes all Grade 7–12 students west to Ruby Creek and up the Fraser Canyon to China Bar — one secondary school for the whole area. Two Rivers Education Centre alternate (Gr.

Services and transit: Fraser Canyon Hospital, 1275 7th Ave, is a 10-bed Fraser Health community hospital with 24/7 emergency stabilization and care, transferring complex cases to Abbotsford Regional Hospital or Royal Columbian Hospital. The Hope & Area Recreation Centre (1005 6th Ave — arena, Dan Sharrers Aquatic Centre, fitness facilities) is managed by the FVRD. Transit is thin: BC Transit Route 72 connects Hope and Agassiz via Highway 7, with onward connections to Chilliwack via Route 71; the FVRD administers the routes and service is a few trips daily.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Hope

items.t: District plans and zoning (District sources only): the current Official Community Plan is OCP Bylaw 1617, 2025, adopted February 9, 2026, updated together with the Zoning Bylaw to meet current provincial housing requirements. The governing zoning bylaw is District of Hope Zoning Bylaw No. 1324, 2012 (consolidated to March 20, 2025); its amendment list includes Bylaw 1580, 2024 (Small Scale Multi-Unit Housing, RS-1 zone, adopted June 10, 2024).

Suite / SSMUH rules: the District's Interim Housing Needs Report (Nov 2024) records that the 2024 SSMUH amendments allow 3 units on parcels under 280 m² and 4 on larger parcels in former 1–2-unit zones, against a calculated 20-year housing need of 2,123 units.

Short-term rentals: Zoning Amendment Bylaw No. 1603, 2025 (adopted September 8, 2025) made short-term rentals a permitted use in designated zones in Hope, and Council voted to opt in to the provincial registry and require a District business licence as of January 1, 2026 — stated here from a secondary summary of the District's bylaws and minutes; confirm the current District guide before relying on fee figures.

Flood rules are a building rule here, not background: the Fraser River's design flood profile is anchored to the Hope gauging station (the 1894 flood, treated as roughly a 500-year event), and new provincial floodplain maps covering the Coquihalla and Fraser rivers from Yale to Mission were released in June 2026. Construction in hazard areas needs a Flood and Erosion Hazards Development Permit — Council (Jan. 13, 2025) approved one for an addition conditional on a satisfactory qualified-professional report — and the District administers the Coquihalla River dikes (River Parade Flood Protection, 0.93 km; Glenhalla Subdivision, 1.01 km). Parcel-level flood construction levels: Not verified.

District taxes — penalty scheme not confirmed: District of Hope municipal taxes plus FVRD levies (recreation is an FVRD service here). The District's tax-rates page records that BC Assessment notices go out each January (value as of July 1 the prior year) and rates must be set before May 15; the 2025 Annual Tax Rate Bylaw is No. 1601, 2025. No other town's scheme is imported (not Mission's, not Chilliwack's).

blocks.text: Good to know about Hope

items.t: Hope got a brand-new OCP in 2026. Official Community Plan Bylaw 1617, 2025 was adopted February 9, 2026, with a companion zoning update — and the District's housing-needs math behind it calculates a 20-year need of 2,123 units, mostly from anticipated growth, in a town that built 70 single-family homes and 22 suites in 2021–Oct 2024.

Park Street Manor turned 50 in 2025. The Hope Standard's July 18, 2025 report marks the manor's 50th anniversary (founded 1975, a Society/provincial/federal partnership) — the town's seniors-housing backbone predates most of its housing stock discussions.

The seniors buildings cluster because the hospital campus anchors them. Fraser Hope Lodge, the Hope Hospice Residence and Fraser Canyon Hospital all sit at 1275 7th Ave, and the Park Street buildings are a few blocks away — Hope's care geography is one walkable townsite node, not scattered sites.

The 2020 inventory is the last full count — treat its numbers as dated. The FVRD's District of Hope inventory (October 2020) is the source behind most unit counts in (Stalo 16, Park Street Manor 21, Riverside 30, Fraser Hope Lodge 50 beds); the Riverstone was still a "proposed" project in it and opened in 2021, which shows how fast a 2020 snapshot ages.

The Othello Tunnels are reopening in phases — check before quoting them. Coquihalla Canyon Provincial Park was damaged at 30+ sites in the November 2021 atmospheric river; phase 1 reopened mid-July 2024 to the end of the second tunnel, the northern portion reopened June 27, 2025 with access to three of five tunnels, and the rest was expected to finish before a spring 2026 full reopening — check the park page for live status.

Hope's median age explains its market (2021 Census): 54.8 years, in a population of 6,686 — yet all of its purpose-built seniors supply is rental or care, so an ownership-minded downsizer is competing for ordinary ranchers and townhomes, not a 55+ product.

items.t: The District of Hope is a district municipality in the Fraser Valley Regional District, at the confluence of the Fraser and Coquihalla rivers, at the eastern end of the Fraser Valley where the Fraser Canyon begins. Its communities include the townsite, Silver Creek, Flood, Kawkawa Lake and Othello. Hope is the junction where the Trans-Canada Highway meets the Fraser Canyon and where Highway 7 (Lougheed) ends; Highway 3 (Hope-Princeton) and Highway 5 (Coquihalla) also branch from Hope.

Board ground: Hope is a CADREB (Chilliwack and District) board community with its own MLS area name, "Hope & Area." CADREB publishes no area statistics and there is no SnapStats coverage — no Hope row exists in the SnapStats FVR September 2026 report. All Hope market figures are not verified from any published stats source and nothing is substituted.

Housing shape: predominantly freehold detached — post-war and 1970s–90s stock in the townsite grid, rancher-style homes in Silver Creek, recreational properties around Kawkawa Lake — with strata a minority share near the core (formal splits not verified), and manufactured homes in parks on the District's fringe. The District's Interim Housing Needs Report (Nov. 2024) records permits 2021–Oct. 2024 as mostly single-family dwellings (70 units) plus suites (22), and a calculated 20-year need of 2,123 units.
Recent build mix and the 2024 SSMUH amendments (3 units on parcels under 280 m², 4 on larger parcels in former 1–2-unit zones) are the District's gentle-density route, not new townhouse complexes.

Schools (SD78 Fraser-Cascade): Coquihalla Elementary (K–6), 455 6th Ave, approximately 350 students; Silver Creek Elementary (K–7) in Silver Creek; Hope Secondary School (Gr. 7–12), 444 Stuart St; Two Rivers Education Centre alternate (Gr. 7–12 students west to Ruby Creek and up the Fraser Canyon to China Bar; Silver Creek's catchment is the Silver Creek area and west of Silver Creek. School names are the Ministry/SD78-listed names.

Transit: BC Transit Route 72 (Hope) connects Hope and Agassiz via Highway 7, with connections onward to Chilliwack via Route 71; the FVRD administers the routes. Service is limited (few trips daily) — Hope is a driving community; schedules must be checked per trip. Timed drives to Chilliwack, Abbotsford and Vancouver: Not verified.

Recreation and health: the Hope & Area Recreation Centre (1005 6th Ave — arena, Dan Sharrers Aquatic Centre, fitness facilities) is managed by the FVRD; Kawkawa Lake, Memorial Park and the Coquihalla Canyon (Othello Tunnels) trail networks are the signature outdoor assets — the tunnels park is being restored in phases after the November 2021 atmospheric river (northern portion reopened June 27, 2025 with access to three of five tunnels; check the BC Parks page for live status). Fraser Canyon Hospital, 1275 7th Ave (Fraser Health), is a 10-bed community hospital with 24/7 emergency stabilization and care.
Nearby areas: Silver Creek and Flood (within the District), Yale, Laidlaw, Agassiz west via Highway 7, Chilliwack west via Highway 1, Boston Bar north up the Fraser Canyon.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Hope

items.t: Form B diligence (the counted stratas): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page.

District plan and zoning: the current plan is Official Community Plan Bylaw 1617, 2025, adopted February 9, 2026, with a companion updated Zoning Bylaw; the OCP and Zoning Bylaw were updated together to meet current provincial housing requirements, and the 2024 SSMUH amendments allow 3 units on parcels under 280 m² and 4 on larger parcels in former 1–2-unit zones.

Flood — the District's first diligence item: the Province's design flood profile for the Fraser River is anchored to the Hope gauging station (the 1894 flood is the design event, treated in updated frequency analysis as roughly a 500-year event), and new provincial floodplain maps covering the Coquihalla and Fraser rivers from Yale to Mission were released in June 2026. The District administers Coquihalla River dikes — River Parade Flood Protection (0.93 km) and Glenhalla Subdivision (1.01 km), both regulated — and construction in hazard areas needs a Flood and Erosion Hazards Development Permit with a satisfactory qualified-professional report (the route Council applied Jan. 13, 2025 at 62180 Delair Road). Parcel-level flood construction levels and any diking/drainage parcel charge: Not verified. Pull the parcel's flood status before pricing or writing — a dike nearby does not remove the permit step.

Tax and levy notes: District of Hope municipal taxes plus FVRD levies (recreation is an FVRD service here); the Annual Tax Rate Bylaw for 2025 is No. 1601, 2025, and Council's finance report (April 28, 2025) finalized the 2025 increase at 2.81% for items the District taxes directly. The July 2 due date for property taxes and residential utilities rests on District notices carried in the local paper and could not be confirmed on a District page pass: Not verified. Utility fees (water/sewer/solid waste) ride on the tax notice, with 5% + 5% late penalties under Utility Bylaw No. 1153 — a utility-bylaw penalty, not a municipal tax-penalty scheme; do not quote it as one.

items.t: Hope is the reference point for Lower Mainland flood planning. The Fraser River's design flood profile is anchored to the Hope gauging station and the 1894 flood is the design event — a Hope buyer is buying inside the measurement system every downstream dike is judged against, which is why the June 2026 provincial floodplain maps for Yale-to-Mission matter here first.
One of Hope's three named complexes cannot say what it is.

The town's largest apartment building cannot be bought. The Riverstone's 37 apartment units plus eight townhouses are all rent-geared-to-income homes (opened July 2, 2021) — Hope's apartment shelf looks bigger in a building count than it is in a buyer count.

Hope's OCP is brand new and already the second plan in two years' conversation. OCP Bylaw 1617, 2025 was adopted February 9, 2026, with a companion Zoning Bylaw and SSMUH rules (3 units under 280 m² lots, 4 on larger) — the gentle-density stock of the next decade here is suites and small multiplexes, not new townhouse complexes.

The tunnels are a phased reopening, not a finished one. Coquihalla Canyon Provincial Park lost 30+ sites and all five Othello Tunnels in November 2021; the northern portion reopened June 27, 2025 reaching three of five tunnels, with the balance expected before a spring 2026 full reopening — check the park page live before quoting trail access in a listing.
Dogwood Place's size is a number nobody should quote.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Hope
What trades here

items.t: What land actually trades here: townsite lots are small-to-standard urban lots; Silver Creek and fringe properties run larger, semi-rural; Kawkawa Lake carries recreational properties.

Fee-simple lots — the default form: predominantly freehold detached per the research; a fee-simple lot carries no strata corporation, no Form B and no strata fees. No bare-land strata lot offered as a vacant lot is verified for this ground.
: Riverwynd's 32 town homes rest on its developer-era launch advertising.

: Timberlane (1275 Scott Drive) is held out of BOTH the townhomes and condos programs on a form conflict — current listings for the same complex disagree on its very form (Row / Townhouse in one, Apartment/Condo in another, with both describing townhouse product, and built 1994 vs 1995). It is documented here on the same basis, counted nowhere as land or as stock; a buyer settles form and plan from the strata documents themselves.

Proposals documented AS SUCH, never as inventory: (1) 62870 Flood Hope Road — OCP Bylaw 1609, 2025 / Zoning Bylaw 1610, 2025, Highway Commercial → Light Industrial and Rural (RU-1) → Light/Service Industrial (I-2); hearing Nov. 24, 2025. (2) 19623 Silver Skagit Road — Bylaws 1598/1599, 2025, Country Residential (CR-1) → Light/Service Industrial (I-2); hearing May 12, 2025. The District publishes no single current-applications list, so these are examples at rezoning stage, not a complete inventory and not lot offerings. BC Housing has also proposed 52 supportive homes at 660/670 Old Hope Princeton Way — a proposal, not stock.

Pad-tenure frame — not lot stock, not land ownership: the District's fringe manufactured-home parks (including Lismore Mobile Home Park, Windmill Park and Crystal River Court on Flood-Hope Road) are pad-rental or leasehold tenancies — a manufactured home on a rented pad is NOT lot stock and NOT land ownership.

ALR edge: some agricultural land exists on the District's fringes (e.g., the Flood/Laidlaw side); the ALR share of the District is not verified — no District OCP or ALC source found states an ALR area or percentage for Hope, so no figure is substituted. ALR status is per-parcel.

Floodplain character: central to this market — the Fraser River's design flood profile is anchored to the Hope gauging station (the 1894 flood, treated as roughly a 500-year event), and new provincial floodplain maps covering the Coquihalla and Fraser rivers from Yale to Mission were released in June 2026.

faq.a: There is no verified apartment-condo building to buy into. Hope's owned strata stock is two townhouse complexes (Riverwynd Estates, Dogwood Place) and one low-rise complex (Timberlane) whose own listings disagree about whether it is townhouse or apartment product — an ownership-minded buyer here is shopping townhouses, ranchers and houses, not apartment condos.
faq.q: Can I buy a condo in Hope?

faq.a: Not confirmed — and that is the honest answer. One current listing calls a unit Row / Townhouse (built 1994); another calls a unit Apartment/Condo (built 1995) while describing the complex as a townhouse. Settle it from the strata plan and Form B for the specific unit before writing.
faq.q: Is Timberlane a condo building or townhouses?

faq.a: No verified one exists. Hope's named strata complexes carry no age restriction in any source found; every purpose-built seniors option in town — Stalo (55+ rental), Park Street Manor (65+), Riverside Manor (assisted/independent rental) — is rental or care, not strata ownership.
faq.q: Is there a 55+ condo or townhouse I can buy in Hope?

faq.a: Stalo Seniors Housing, 541 Park St: 16 units run by the Coquihalla Intercare Society, recorded by the FVRD's 2020 inventory as "for seniors 55 years of age and older." Current availability, rents and subsidy status are not confirmed — contact the operator directly.
faq.q: What is the actual 55+ rental option in Hope?

faq.a: You own the home and rent the pad. Lismore (87 pads) is called a "Senior's mobile home park" and Windmill (13 pads) "for seniors" in the FVRD inventory, but neither source states the exact age — get the park rules in writing before buying a home in either. Pad rent increases are capped under the MHPTA (2026: 2.3% + proportional; 2027: 2.2% + proportional).
faq.q: How do the seniors manufactured-home parks work — do I own anything?

faq.q: Is Timberlane a condo building or townhouses?

faq.a: Not verified from any published stats source: CADREB publishes board-wide statistics only and SnapStats has no Hope row. The micro-markets — townsite, Silver Creek, Kawkawa Lake, Flood/Laidlaw acreages — price and appraise differently; do not blend comparables across them.
faq.q: What are Hope homes worth / how is the market?

faq.a: Parts of the District are Fraser/Coquihalla floodplain, the Fraser's design flood is measured at the Hope gauge, updated provincial floodplain maps for this reach were released in June 2026, and builds/additions in hazard areas need a Flood and Erosion Hazards Development Permit with a qualified-professional report. Check the specific parcel against the maps before writing.
faq.q: Is flooding a real issue for a Hope townhouse?

faq.a: No — no named acreage subdivision, bare-land strata acreage community or presale lot offering was verified. Land trades parcel by parcel: townsite lots, larger semi-rural Silver Creek and fringe parcels, and Kawkawa Lake recreational properties — and those micro-markets are never blended for pricing.
faq.q: Is there an acreage subdivision to buy into in Hope?

faq.a: Yes, parcel by parcel. The Fraser's design flood is the 1894 event measured at the Hope gauge, new provincial floodplain maps for this reach were released June 2026, and construction in hazard areas needs a Flood and Erosion Hazards Development Permit with a qualified-professional report — a dike nearby (River Parade, Glenhalla) does not remove the permit step. Parcel-level flood construction levels: Not verified until the parcel is checked.
faq.q: Is flooding a real issue for a Hope parcel?

faq.a: The 2024 SSMUH amendments allow 3 units on parcels under 280 m² and 4 on larger parcels in former 1–2-unit zones — gentle density on serviced lots, not an acreage-subdivision route. On ALR land the ALC rules govern instead.
faq.q: Can a townsite lot add units under the new rules?

faq.a: What trades here is predominantly freehold detached houses; a duplex on a single lot sells whole.
faq.q: Is there any half duplex for sale in Hope?

faq.a: Only if a strata plan or a subdivided lot gives that side its own title. Without one there is no separate half to buy.
faq.q: A listing calls a Hope home a duplex — can I buy one side?
